title: Cofibrant simplicial inversion is base change of total groupoid completion
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, the Bergner structure, object-preserving replacement $R$ and $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Fix a small set $O$ of objects and let $i:A\to B$ be a cofibration between cofibrant simplicial categories with object set $O$, identity on objects. Let $G(A)=A[A^{-1}]$ be obtained by groupoid-completing the ordinary category in each simplicial degree. Let $B[A^{-1}]$ denote degreewise inversion of the images of arrows of $A$. The ordinary pushout square of simplicial categories
$$\begin{array}{ccc} A&\longrightarrow&G(A)\\ \downarrow i&&\downarrow\\ B&\longrightarrow&B[A^{-1}]\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pushout for the Bergner homotopy theory. Equivalently, replacing the span by a cofibrant span and taking its pushout gives a Dwyer--Kan equivalence to this displayed pushout. The simplicial map
$$\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)\longrightarrow\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(G(A))$$
induced by total inversion is a weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets and its target is a Kan complex. These assertions are natural in maps of the cofibrant pairs. They impose no requirement that the image of $A$ be saturated or satisfy two-out-of-three in $B$.

source.place: Sections 7.2-7.6 (fixed-object model structure and cofibrations), 8.1-8.2 (homotopy meaning of pushout), 9.1-9.2 (cofibrant groupoid completion), 10.1 and 10.3 (cofibrant localization), printed pp.276-281. The Bergner/coherent-nerve formulation is the derived-inversion formulation in Hinich Section 1.2, printed pp.5-6, especially its paragraph citing DK1 9.2 and its cocartesian diagram (5). This is the unsaturated cofibrant-pair version; the subsequent saturated-marking Proposition 1.2.1 is not used as a black box. No Stacks tag states these enriched assertions.

proof.text: Write $C=G(A)$ and let $j:A\to C$ be total inversion. For any simplicial category $T$, a functor $B\to T$ extends across degreewise inversion exactly when it carries every degreewise arrow in the image of $A$ to an invertible arrow in the corresponding ordinary category $T_n$. In that case its restriction to $A$ extends uniquely to $C$, by sending each formal inverse to the inverse of its image. These extensions commute with all simplicial operators, since functors preserve inverses uniquely. Thus the displayed square is the ordinary pushout, computed in fixed-object simplicial categories and also in all simplicial categories. This universal-property argument also applies to targets whose object set differs from $O$: both legs specify the same object function.

source.place: Section 3.1 ordinary inversion universal property and Section 9.1 degreewise completion; direct word argument

proof.text:
Here is the bar augmentation calculation, with an arbitrary second leg $A\to C_0$ and with $i:A\to B$ fixed. Use the coproduct $*$ and the strong free retract description of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus]. Form the bisimplicial category $T_r=B*A^{*r}*C_0$ for $r\geq0$, augmented to $P=B\amalg_A C_0$. Bar faces fold adjacent copies of $A$, or fold the end copy into $B$ or $C_0$ by the two structure maps; degeneracies insert a new $A$ factor by the identity-only unit, so their maps omit that factor. All identities follow on each coproduct factor, and hence on words.

First suppose $i$ is free. Fix the original simplicial degree $q$, so $B_q=F_q*A_q$ and $P_q=F_q*(C_0)_q$. In bar degree $r$ write $(T_r)_q=F_q*A_0*\cdots*A_r*(C_0)_q$, where the subscripts $0,\ldots,r$ label copies of $A_q$. Define an extra degeneracy by fixing $F_q,(C_0)_q$ and sending the copy $A_k$ into copy $A_{k+1}$, leaving copy $A_0$ unused. The degree-minus-one section includes $F_q*(C_0)_q$ and omits $A_0$. Explicitly, $d_i$ folds copies $A_i,A_{i+1}$ for $0\leq i<r$ and $d_r$ folds $A_r$ into $(C_0)_q$; $s_i$ inserts an unused copy $A_{i+1}$, sending $A_k$ to $A_k$ for $k\leq i$ and to $A_{k+1}$ for $k>i$. Write $h_r$ for the shift and $h_{-1}$ for the section. Then $d_0h_r=1$, since folding copies $0,1$ sends the shifted copy $A_{k+1}$ back to $A_k$. Also $d_1h_0=h_{-1}\varepsilon_0$, since both sides send the original $A_0$ into $(C_0)_q$. For $0\leq i\leq r+1$, $d_{i+1}h_{r+1}=h_rd_i$: the adjacent copies folded on either side have original labels $i,i+1$, and in the last-face case both sides send the last copy into $(C_0)_q$. For $0\leq i\leq r$, $s_{i+1}h_r=h_{r+1}s_i$: both sides send $A_k$ to $A_{k+1}$ if $k\leq i$ and to $A_{k+2}$ if $k>i$. All these maps fix $F_q,(C_0)_q$, and $\varepsilon_0h_{-1}=1$. Hence they satisfy exactly the extra-degeneracy identities. For each pair $x,y$, [lem-coef-extra-degeneracy-contraction] gives a section and simplicial homotopy for the augmented bar set of arrows. Its realization is a homotopy equivalence: realize the prism homotopy on each simplex; its two composites are the identity and the section followed by the augmentation. Hence this is a weak homotopy equivalence. Applying [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to the two simplicial degrees of each mapping set proves $\operatorname{diag}T\to P$ is a local weak equivalence. The degreewise free decompositions need not be compatible with faces in $q$, since the diagonal theorem only needs this rowwise assertion. For a general cofibration $i$, take its strong free retract, keep $A,C_0$ fixed and form the same bars and pushouts. Their augmentations exhibit the original augmentation as a retract of the free one, so it is again a local weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 8.2 proof, pp.278-279; explicit missing contraction written here using Mathlib ExtraDegeneracy.homotopy

proof.text: If $C_1\to C_0$ is a local weak equivalence under $A$, [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] makes every map $B*A^{*r}*C_1\to B*A^{*r}*C_0$ a local weak equivalence, by repeated binary free-product invariance. For each $x,y$ apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] in the original simplicial degree to obtain a local weak equivalence between the diagonal bars. Their augmentations to the two pushouts are local weak equivalences by step 2. The augmentation square commutes factor by factor, so two-out-of-three makes $B\amalg_A C_1\to B\amalg_A C_0$ a local weak equivalence. This argument concerns an arbitrary replacement of the second leg, not an assumption about total inversion preserving local weak equivalences.

source.place: Propositions 2.7 and 8.1-8.2, pp.270-271,278-279; explicit comparison of the two augmented bars

proof.text: Apply the functorial fixed-object factorization of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] to $j:A\to C=G(A)$, writing $A\hookrightarrow\widetilde C\xrightarrow{p}C$, with $p$ a trivial fibration. The hypotheses on $A,B,i$ give fixed-object cofibrancy and a fixed-object cofibration by the same node. For the direct Reedy category with arrows $a\to b,a\to c$, [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] says that the span $B\leftarrow A\to\widetilde C$ is cofibrant: the latching conditions are exactly cofibrancy of $A$ and cofibrancy of its two outgoing maps. The same conditions hold in the Bergner model structure by the fixed-object/Bergner agreement. Thus its ordinary pushout is a pushout of a cofibrant span computing the homotopy pushout in the sense stipulated in the statement. Step 3 applied to $p$ shows that the comparison $B\amalg_A\widetilde C\to B\amalg_A C=B[A^{-1}]$ is a local weak equivalence. It fixes $O$, so its induced functor on $\pi_0$ is fully faithful and surjective on objects, hence it is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. This proves the homotopy-pushout assertion in the Bergner, rather than only the fixed-object, homotopy theory.

source.place: Sections 7.2-7.6 and Proposition 8.1; direct Reedy cofibrant-span interpretation

proof.text: Let $D(V)=\operatorname{diag}_{p,q}N_p(V_q)$. Cofibrancy of $A$ and [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] give a retract $A\to E\to A$ with $E_q$ free for every $q$. Apply degreewise groupoid completion and ordinary nerve to this retraction. For every $q$, the canonical $N(E_q)\to N(G(E_q))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-free-category-groupoid-nerve]. Consequently $N(A_q)\to N(G(A_q))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, as a retract of that map. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence], now to the degreewise ordinary nerves, to conclude that $D(A)\to D(G(A))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The two uses of a diagonal in steps 2 and 5 are distinct: step 2 uses mapping sets of a bar of simplicial categories, whereas this step uses nerves of ordinary categories.

source.place: Proposition 9.2 proof from Proposition 7.6 and Proposition 3.7, pp.272,278-279

proof.text: For $V=A$ and $V=G(A)$ use the natural weak homotopy equivalence $z_V:D(V)\to D(RV)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RV)$ in [lem-coef-diagonal-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The comparison theorem is applied only to the locally Kan objects $RV$. Naturality gives the commutative square with upper edge $D(A)\to D(G(A))$, lower edge $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RA)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RG(A))$, and vertical edges $z_A,z_{G(A)}$. All but the lower edge are weak homotopy equivalences by step 5 and the cited comparison. Two-out-of-three proves that the lower edge is a weak homotopy equivalence. By the specified definition of $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}$, this is precisely the map in the statement, rather than an unrelated equivalence of homotopy types.

source.place: Definition 1.7, Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 4.3, printed pp.31,33-34,40, applied after locally Kan replacement

proof.text: The ordinary category $G(A)_0$ is a groupoid. Every arrow representing a morphism of $\pi_0G(A)$ is represented by a vertex of a mapping set; its inverse in $G(A)_0$ represents an inverse of its component. Thus $\pi_0G(A)$ is a groupoid. The object-preserving local weak equivalence $G(A)\to RG(A)$ induces bijections on all such component sets, respecting composition and identities, so $\pi_0RG(A)$ is also a groupoid. It is locally Kan by construction. The last clause of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] now gives that $N_{\mathrm{hc}}RG(A)$ is Kan, as required.

source.place: Proposition 1.2.5.1 and the locally Kan coherent-nerve criterion of the cited node

proof.text: Total inversion is a functor: send a formal inverse of an arrow to the inverse of its image. The pushout identification of step 1 commutes with this formula. The bar comparison is induced on every coproduct factor and its augmentation, so it commutes with maps of the pairs; the fixed-object factorization can be functorial by [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus]. The retractions and degreewise free decompositions above are used only to verify weak equivalences, not to define any of the maps claimed in the statement. Finally $R$ is functorial and $z_V$ is natural by [lem-coef-diagonal-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Thus both the pushout square and the total-inversion map have the asserted naturality. All arguments applied to an arbitrary cofibration $A\to B$; none used saturation or two-out-of-three for its image.

source.place: Functoriality of ordinary inversion and bars; the stated functoriality of replacement and of the nerve comparison

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged. Proved the ordinary pushout by inverse words; established bar augmentation by an explicit extra degeneracy and free retracts, compared replacement bars and a Bergner-cofibrant span, then proved the ordinary diagonal-nerve completion equivalence using free ordinary categories and passed to derived coherent nerves through a separate locally Kan comparison. Four new statement-only nodes, one an exact Mathlib leaf. No saturation assumption, attachment, Lean writing or compilation. Second reading corrected printed Arakawa page references, made bar index identities explicit, and clarified two inline definitions; independent searches confirm the existing leaf classification.

DK I is not in literature/ and the network is blocked; I read a local copy at /tmp/dk1src at 1.4(ii)-(vii), 2.5-2.9, 3.1-3.8, 7.1-7.6, 8.1-8.3 and 9.1-9.7. Checked against DK I: free-product invariance with no cofibrancy (2.7), free maps and strong free retracts (7.4-7.6), the bar with i copies of A (8.2, whose proof omits the contraction), and groupoid completion of cofibrant V (9.2, proved from 7.6 and 3.7). Step 2: I checked by hand every extra-degeneracy identity of the shift A_k->A_{k+1}, including d_0h=1, d_1h_0=h_{-1}eps_0, the face/shift identities case by case and the degeneracy/shift identities. They match the Mathlib ExtraDegeneracy fields at lines 72-83. The leaf ExtraDegeneracy.section_/section_comp_hom/homotopy (lines 126/142/174) is stated for any category C, so C=Type is a one-line specialization. Steps 3-7 use only what the cited nodes state: the diagonal theorem in both directions, Reedy latching for the span, R and N_hc applied only to locally Kan objects, and the groupoid-pi_0 Kan clause. Steps 1 and 8 are elementary. All proof citations lie in the unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general; no tool_uses are needed. I could not open Arakawa or HTT, so I checked those claims directly. For agreement of fixed-object and Bergner cofibrations: trivial fibrations in sCat_O are Bergner trivial fibrations, and a Bergner trivial fibration pulled back along O->Ob P is one in sCat_O; the same holds for cofibrant objects. For the diagonal comparison: I built a natural map C[Delta^n]->F_n (an n-simplex of D(A) is a functor F_n->A), sending S to max{s in S : s<=k-1}, so D(A)->N_hc(A) exists. Local invariance is DK 1.4(vii). Small cases checked: discrete A, a one-object simplicial group, a free category with one or two loops, empty O, A=I_O, i=id. A full-DAG duplicate scan found nothing: the dk-cofibrant-localization, hammock, partial-sum-bar and simplicial-groupoid-localization nodes state different things. No new node restates a clause of the item, and none carries a proof. Fields and blueprint refs are correct. No SGA source; no target or base-change morphism involved. No fixes made.
